ddx.step1_summary:
• Chief complaint: “Crazy” headache for 3 days
• Symptom details:
  – Onset/duration: began ~3 days ago, gradually worsened
  – Location: global but maximal around right eye
  – Character: dull baseline, intermittently sharper; constant with fluctuations
  – Severity: 8/10
  – Associated: photophobia (light hurts), transient “shooting lights” at onset, nausea (no vomiting), difficulty concentrating
  – Aggravating/alleviating: ibuprofen (3 tabs/day) not helpful; sleep did not help; screen brightness reduced
  – No fever, neck stiffness, focal weakness, speech difficulty, trauma, rash
• Past medical history: none reported; no prior migraines
• Medications/allergies: no regular meds; no known drug allergies
• Family history: mother and sister have frequent migraines
• Social history: 26-y-o female; IT job with heavy computer use; lives with 3 housemates; social smoker and social alcohol use; mild work stress; wears glasses since age 5
• Vital signs / exam: not provided (tele-visit)
• Labs/imaging: none mentioned

V: Subarachnoid hemorrhage: acute severe headache with photophobia can be concerning for SAH, though onset here was gradual rather than thunderclap
Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis: young female, headache, ocular-area pain; but no risk factors (OCP, pregnancy) documented
I: Viral or bacterial meningitis: headache, photophobia, nausea; lack of fever/neck stiffness argues against but still possible
Acute sinusitis: periorbital/right-eye predominant pain could reflect frontal/ethmoid sinus inflammation
N: Intracranial mass/brain tumor: progressive headache, worse in morning could occur; no focal deficits but still on list
D: Tension-type headache: bilateral band-like dull pain linked to stress and screen use
I2: Medication-overuse headache: daily NSAID use for consecutive days, though duration short (≤3 d) makes this less likely
C: Chiari malformation type I: can present with sub-occipital headaches exacerbated by Valsalva; no clear triggers here
A: Idiopathic intracranial hypertension (IIH): young woman, ocular pain, visual phenomena, photophobia
T: Post-traumatic headache: ruled out by absence of head injury
E: Migraine with aura: unilateral-predominant, photophobia, visual scintillations, nausea, family history

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Classic migraine profile: unilateral-predominant, moderate-to-severe intensity, photophobia, visual ‘shooting lights’, nausea, female in 20s, strong family history. Lack of response to single-tablet ibuprofen and functional impairment also typical.
supporting_evidence: Prior headaches relieved by NSAID; current episode more severe and prolonged—common in evolving migraine pattern
opposing_evidence: Headache described as constant for 3 days rather than discrete attacks

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Stress, prolonged computer use, dull constant pain could reflect tension headache, which is common and can be refractory to low-dose NSAID if severe.
supporting_evidence: Diffuse, dull pain present ‘all over head’
opposing_evidence: Photophobia and visual aura less typical for tension headache
Severity rated 8/10 (often milder in tension headaches)

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Periorbital/right-eye pain can stem from sinus inflammation; may worsen over days and be unrelieved by simple analgesics.
opposing_evidence: No nasal congestion, rhinorrhea, fever or facial tenderness reported

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Young women can present with persistent headache and visual disturbances; however, no obesity, pulsatile tinnitus, or documented papilledema.
supporting_evidence: Headache with visual disturbances and photophobia
opposing_evidence: No obesity or OCP use stated
No transient visual obscurations or double vision
No exam findings of papilledema (not examined)

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: SAH can cause severe photophobic headache, but classic presentation is sudden thunderclap; absence of abrupt onset or neurological deficits makes SAH unlikely but serious enough to consider if condition changes.
opposing_evidence: No neck stiffness, focal deficits, or vomiting
